description: Morgan Life OS — Personalized suggestion pool. Level 1 = Health, Level 2 = Safety, Level 3 = Connection. All tasks designed for POTS, cervical/lumbar spine issues, ADHD, anxiety, and real life in 2026.

suggestions.text: Drink 8–16 oz of salty fluid right now (broth, LMNT, V8, or salted water).
Mix tomorrow's electrolyte bottle and put it in the fridge so it's ready.
Lay out your compression socks somewhere visible so you'll put them on before standing for long.
Pre-load before leaving: drink a salty drink 20–30 minutes before you need to drive or be upright.
Open your POTS protocol and pick just one step you can honor today.
Do 2 minutes of gentle SCM pinch-and-lift (no tools, no force — just fingers).
Do 3 chin tucks lying down: pull chin gently toward throat, hold 5 seconds, release. Repeat 3×.
Check your posture right now: is your neck craned forward? Adjust your pillow, monitor, or seat by even 1 inch.
Apply a heating pad or warm pack to the base of your skull for 5–10 minutes.
Apply a lidocaine strip or small Voltaren dab to your worst trigger point (stay within safety rules).
Try the gentle hair-pull technique for 30 seconds on one spot to ease allodynia.
Take today's regular meds or BC — the ones you might skip when distracted.
It's an iron day — take your iron with a vitamin C source, away from calcium or coffee.
Mark your iron status somewhere visible (the app, a note, your planner) — even just 'done' or 'skip'.
Pre-fill tomorrow's meds in a small dish or pillbox right now.
Take one supportive supplement (magnesium, B12, zinc, etc.) — just one, not the whole stack.
Turn on your screen's blue-light filter or put on blue blockers — aim to do it before 9 PM.
Dim the lights and silence notifications for 15 minutes to start winding down.
Rate last night's sleep 1–5 and note one thing that might improve tonight.
Do 3 rounds of box breathing: inhale 4 sec → hold 4 → exhale 4 → hold 4.
Turn on a calming background sound (rain, fan, white noise) for 10 minutes and just sit.
Ask Dom to be nearby while you do one small task, or put on a body-doubling stream.
Set a 5-minute timer and do anything from your list until it rings. Stop when it rings — no guilt.
Give yourself a 3-minute nothing buffer between tasks — scroll, stretch, stare at the wall. It counts.
Move one important thing (meds, water bottle, your phone) somewhere impossible to ignore.
Write the single next step you need to take on a sticky note and put it somewhere you'll see it.
Do a 2-minute gentle stretch (neck, shoulders, hips) between sitting blocks. Set a timer.
Walk to the mailbox or the end of the driveway and back, noticing your feet touching the ground.
Stand outside for 3–5 minutes and let yourself actually notice the light and air.
Look at one tree, cloud, or plant for 60 seconds and just notice it.
Play one song and sway, stretch, or just move in place. No choreography required.
Check your car's dashboard: any warning lights on? If yes, snap a photo so you remember to look it up.
Check your gas gauge. If it's at ¼ or below, add 'get gas' to today or tomorrow — don't let it creep to empty.
Step outside and eyeball your tires for obvious low pressure or uneven wear.
Snap a photo of your odometer or jot the mileage in your car log.
Pop your trunk and peek at your emergency kit (blanket, jumper cables, snack, water). Add one missing item if you have it.
Look up one mechanic near you and save their name and number in your phone or notes.
Open your banking app and look at your balance and pending charges — no decisions needed, just awareness.
Find one bill email you've been avoiding and either pay it, schedule it, or move it to a clearly-labeled 'Bills' folder.
Scan your last card statement for one subscription you don't recognize or don't use — flag it for later.
Label one budget category (Gas, Groceries, Meds) even if you don't fill in numbers yet. One label is a win.
Move even $5–$20 into a separate buffer or emergency sub-account if you're able to today.
Pick up the top 3 papers from your pile and sort them: trash, file, or action. You don't have to finish the pile.
Open one piece of mail you've been avoiding. Decide: trash, keep, or needs action.
Add one upcoming appointment, refill date, or kid event into your main calendar.
Update or save one password into your password manager.
Delete or file 5 random icons or screenshots from your computer desktop.
Check that your phone photos are auto-backing up — or manually back up today's photos.
Skim 3 job listings that fit your health criteria (remote, flexible posture) — just read them, no applying required.
Reread your health-first job criteria list to remind yourself what you will and won't accept. You set those rules for a reason.
Set up or tweak one job alert on LinkedIn or Indeed (keywords + remote filter).
Add one job you're considering to your tracker — even just the company name and role.
Update one bullet on your resume or LinkedIn headline to better match your real target roles.
Add one sentence, bullet, or screenshot to your portfolio. 10 minutes max — done is better than perfect.
Grab visible trash from one room into a bag and move it to the door. Done.
Set a 2-minute timer and clear one surface (desk, nightstand, coffee table). Stop when it rings.
Bring any cups, plates, or bowls from bedroom or office to the kitchen sink.
Start one laundry load. No obligation to fold today — future you can handle that.
Before bed, check that the doors and windows you care about are locked.
Give Dom a full 10–20 second hug when you're near each other. No words required — just hold.
As you walk past Dom, put a hand on his arm or shoulder for a second, then keep going.
Sit in the same room as Dom for 5 minutes while he does his thing. No talking needed — just share space.
Name one specific thing Dom did today that helped you, out loud. ('Thanks for making coffee earlier' counts.)
Ask Dom: 'What was a high, a low, and one thing you need today?' Share yours too. No fixing — just listen.
Ask Dom one question about something he's into right now ('How's that game? What's that video about?') and accept whatever answer you get.
Suggest doing three slow box breaths together before bed or before you both sit down. It's 90 seconds total.
Watch what Eli's doing (game, YouTube, whatever) from the couch or doorway for 3 minutes without commenting. Just notice his world.
Say: 'You look really focused on that' or 'You seem really into that' — without asking him to stop or perform.
Mentally note (or jot in your notes) one topic Eli seems animated about lately. This is research for future connection bids.
Bring Eli a drink or snack, say 'Here's a thing if you want it,' and walk away. No strings attached.
Put Eli's favorite blanket or snack somewhere he'll notice it, without mentioning it. Warmth doesn't always need words.
Say 'I'm glad you're here' or 'I like living with you' as you walk by Eli. No follow-up needed.
Ask Eli one question about what he's currently into: 'What's that game about?' or 'Who's your favorite character lately?' Drop it after whatever answer you get.
Tell Eli: 'I'm going to do X — you're welcome to join if you feel like it, totally no pressure.' This counts whether he says yes or no.
Tell Eli: 'If you feel like hanging out for 10 minutes later tonight, come find me — I'd like that.' Don't bring it up again.
If Eli starts talking today, stay in the conversation 2–3 extra minutes before redirecting. Let him lead.
If Eli comes to your room or workspace, put your phone down and give him your full attention for those few minutes.
Offer Eli: 'I've got 10 minutes to just listen about anything you want — no advice, no fixing, I promise.' It's okay if he says 'nah.'
Spend 5–10 minutes browsing one Buffalo, ADHD, or chronic-illness group online. Save any names that look 'not awful' in your Reference.
Read one 'looking for friends' or 'new in town' thread on r/Buffalo. Just a reminder you're not the only one rebuilding.
Click into one local meetup or event page (introverts group, game night, self-help group) and skim the description. Zero RSVP required.
If your nervous system is okay with it, tap 'join' on one online group that looks gentle. No posting required.
Write yourself one kind sentence about how you coped today. It still counts as connection — with the most important person.
